newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said a DGII official would brief reporters on practical aspects of the euro at 1215/1015 GMT on Wednesday.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said the Commission was currently studying the final report of the high-level expert group on "Building the European information society for us all". Nolan said it would take it into account when finalising its follow-up to the green paper on "Living and working in the information society: people first" by the end of June.

Van der Pas said the Commission had received the World Trade Organisation's final report on hormones. He said the Commission was highly disappointed by the report. "The panel has not sufficiently taken into account the scientific elements put forward by the European Union and the Union is worried by larger implications of the panel's conclusions that seem to undermine rights for each Member State to establish the level of protection for their consumers," van der Pas said.
Spokesman Gerry Kiely added that the EU would appeal the decision within 41 days and that the procedure implied that a new panel would then be created after 60 or 90 days.

Spokesman Peter Jorgensen said Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard considered that there were too many infringements in the field of environment and that there was no reason why the Commission would not increase the use of penalty payments under article 171 of the EU Treaty against a member state that has not complied with a Court of Justice judgment.
Jorgensen said the results of the Second Earth Summit held in New York City last week were not as bad as might have been expected.

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Global Information Networks Conference to take place in Bonn next Monday and Tuesday. He said it would gather ministers from the 15 Member States, European Free Trade Association, central and eastern European countries, U.S., Canada, Russia and Japan. Kubosch said he expected a ministerial declaration on Internet minimum regulation, tax neutrality, content responsibility on the Internet, networks data protection and security and other issues.

- IP/97/584: Commission takes legal action against Spain, Portugal and Italy on nature conservation, animal protection and impact assessment.
- IP/97/585: Commission takes legal action against Portugal and Austria on air pollution.
- IP/97/586: EU/Ivory Coast fisheries agreement renewal.
- IP/97/587: EU makes new WTO offer on financial services.
- IP/97/588: Information Society: final report of the high level group of experts.

- IP/97/591: Commission approves the acquisition of joint control of Crediop by the banking group Dexia and San Paolo.
- IP/97/592: Commission authorises acquisition of German SPAR Handels AG by French group ITM.
- Speech/97/148: Speech by Commission Presdident Jacques Santer on "external aspects of the euro".
- Speech/97/149: Speech by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on "preparing the euro: where do we stand 500 days before the deadline".
